deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page defines, for an operator A in a von Neumann algebra with a trace T, the decreasing rearrangement φ_{|A|} of |A| (its singular-value function). It then defines a determinant Δ_A(t) = exp ∫_0^t log φ_{|A|}(s) ds, and Δ(A) = Δ_A(ω) when ω = T(1) < ∞. This is the Fuglede–Kadison determinant written through the rearrangement function. The previous page also starts the commutative case E = C_0(M), where atoms t ∈ M carry point masses. This page, though heavily struck through and only partly legible, appears to carry out a structural decomposition.

Points t of the spectrum Ω of the centre with positive mass give central projections U_{t}. These satisfy U_{t}E = EU_{t} = E, i.e. the projection E lies under the central support U_{t}. Using them, A splits as a direct sum of two parts:
- A_1, the 'atomic' part: a direct sum of factors A_i = U_{t} A U_{t} of type I, each isomorphic to some L(H), carrying minimal projections E with T(E) < +∞.
- A_2, the 'diffuse' part: no minimal projections.

There is a fragment about a bound 'EF ≤ c b' with b in the centre C (a centre-valued estimate). The commutative analogue is the split of a measure into atoms (μ({t}) > 0) and a diffuse part. The bottom lines restate this: 'Soit I l'ensemble des t ∈ Ω (isolés) … du centre C de A tels que les sous-algèbres A_i = U_{t} A U_{t} de A soient de type I, i.e. admettent une projection minimale.'

Purpose: to handle jumps of φ_A (discrete spectrum and multiplicities given by traces of minimal projections) separately from the continuous part, when developing rearrangement inequalities and determinants. The next page reduces the general case to a diffuse algebra by tensoring with L^∞[0,1] (T(f) = ∫_0^1 T(f(s)) ds). This is standard preparatory material for Grothendieck's 1955 Bourbaki exposé on rearrangements in von Neumann algebras with a trace.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. Most of the page is struck through or illegible, so the arguments cannot be checked in detail.
The decomposition into an atomic type-I part with minimal projections plus a diffuse part is correct for von Neumann algebras with a faithful normal semifinite trace.

ideas.what: Splitting a traced von Neumann algebra into a part generated by minimal projections (a sum of type I factors L(H) over atoms of the centre) and a diffuse part without minimal projections
ideas.modern_name: Atomic/diffuse decomposition of a von Neumann algebra; discrete type I summand
ideas.where_published: Possibly used implicitly in 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace', Sém. Bourbaki exp. 113 (1955)

ideas.what: Determinant via the singular-value rearrangement function (on the previous page), with atoms giving jumps
ideas.modern_name: Fuglede–Kadison determinant expressed through generalized s-numbers μ_t(A)
ideas.where_published: Sém. Bourbaki exp. 113 (1955), on rearrangements in von Neumann algebras with trace

deep.surprise_reason: Routine structural lemma (atomic vs. diffuse summands with minimal projections). It serves Grothendieck's 1953–55 work on rearrangement functions and determinants, which is published in his Bourbaki exposé and later rediscovered and developed by Fack–Kosaki. No new idea is legible.
